title: Add RAG contract-orchestrator quickstart with deterministic cache probes
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Context: teams building RAG-based agents want a repeatable pattern for contract-first orchestration (tool contracts + staged retrieval) that is easy to run locally and in CI. This quickstart introduces a small orchestrator scaffold that wires a contract schema to a tool-calling runtime, adds deterministic cache probe harnesses, and includes a compact smoke-suite for regressions. Motivation: improve onboarding for platform teams and provide a reproducible baseline for telemetry/latency trade-offs when KV cache/multi-stage retrieval are used.

What this PR does: adds a new quickstart under quickstarts/rag-contract-orchestrator that demonstrates: 1) a contract-first tool interface (OpenAPI-lite JSON contracts used by the orchestrator), 2) staged retrieval pipeline (metadata filter -> sparse index -> dense fallback), 3) deterministic KV-cache probes to exercise cache hit/miss paths for stable e2e assertions, 4) a CI smoke-suite that runs the orchestrator with recorded index fixtures and an ephemeral in-memory tool shim.

Checklist: - [x] Add quickstart scaffold and README with run instructions - [x] Implement orchestrator example (node/ts) + contract JSONs - [x] Add deterministic cache probe harness and fixtures - [x] Add CI smoke job and GitHub Actions workflow - [x] Document expected telemetry events and sample dashboards - [x] Add smoke assertions for cost token counts and latency buckets

How to run locally: 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/rag-contract-orchestrator 2) npm ci && npm run build 3) npm run start:fixture (loads small index and starts in-memory tool shims) 4) npm run smoke (runs the deterministic probe suite and emits a JSON summary under out/smoke-summary.json)

Notes on deterministic probes: the harness seeds the KV cache and retrieval order using a 64-bit deterministic RNG seed so replaying the harness in CI produces identical cache hit/miss traces. Tests assert on token usage bands and one-hot telemetry events (cache_hit, cache_fill, retrieval_fallback). This makes the quickstart suitable as a reproducible scenario for performance regression alerts.

Commits summary: - Create initial quickstart scaffold and README - Implement orchestrator runtime and contract loader - Add cache-probe harness and recorded fixtures - Add GitHub Actions workflow and CI smoke step - Small lint/docs fixes after review

Changed areas (high level): - quickstarts/rag-contract-orchestrator/README.md - quickstarts/rag-contract-orchestrator/src/orchestrator.ts - quickstarts/rag-contract-orchestrator/src/contracts/*.json - quickstarts/rag-contract-orchestrator/test/probes/* - .github/workflows/quickstarts-smoke.yml - docs/quickstarts/index.md (cross-link)

Review conversation (high level): Reviewer: Miguel Santos: "Nice shape — can we simplify the contract JSONs to focus on required fields only? Also please add a short note about privacy (fixtures contain fake PII)." 
Author (Priya): "Agreed — trimmed contract payloads and added a privacy section to the README noting synthetic fixture data and how to swap in customer indexes for Private deployments." 
Reviewer: Ava Lin: "CI flaked once on Linux smoke (timeout). Can we increase the Action timeout for the smoke step and add a rerun comment?" 
Author: "Raised timeout to 30m for smoke job and added retry: 2 on the workflow step." 
Reviewer: Jonah Becker: "Can we add a tiny example showing how to wire this orchestrator to Redwood API streaming responses?" 
Author: "Added snippet in README and a link to the SDK usage (TS) — left streaming as an extension for follow-up to avoid making the quickstart bigger."

CI details: initial run: lint/pass, unit tests/pass, smoke/fail (timeout on Linux runner) -> re-run after bumping timeout -> all checks pass. Coverage: smoke suite covers orchestrator happy path and cache-hit/miss asserts; the quickstart intentionally keeps heavy network calls mocked to keep CI stable.

Merge: merged by squash into main. Merge method: squash. Post-merge actions: updated quickstarts index page and scheduled a short workshop in the internal docs guild to show the pattern next week.
